what: REGISTRY_MODEL.md and eval/op_template.py define validate() as SUPPORTED-then-EXCLUSIONS but never say where MALFORMED-REQUEST checks (ValueError/RuntimeError) go relative to the support gate. The template puts them first, and for any op with an opt-in argument that is itself a gated axis (padding here; equally an alignment/scale/mode kwarg elsewhere) that ordering is WRONG: golden_harness.py:63 decorates out-of-SUPPORTED cells xfail(strict, raises=NotImplementedError), so a pre-gate ValueError on an unsupported axis value lands in xfail_wrong_mode rather than xfail_expected. 83 of this op cells hit it. The resolution is not obvious either, because the immutable acceptance test demands (ValueError, RuntimeError) for the same call - it only works because NotImplementedError is a subclass of RuntimeError, which nothing states.
suggest: In REGISTRY_MODEL.md validate() section, split malformed-request checks into UNCONDITIONAL (illegal under every future SUPPORTED: wrong layout, not on device, impossible tile geometry -> before the gate) and SUPPORT-CONDITIONAL (a complaint about an argument belonging to a gated axis -> AFTER the gate, so it re-arms when the axis is added). Add the one-line fact that SupportRefusal < NotImplementedError < RuntimeError, so an acceptance test matching (ValueError, RuntimeError) is satisfied by a support refusal.

what: no_axes_found is absent from the verifier prompt category table and verify_supported.py renders it as a benign warning (likely test_regression.py - not driven by the registry). For this op that bucket was 475 rows and CONCEALED a total failure: the externally-authored graded suite test_golden_main_tests.py dispatches through ttnn.tilize, which did not exist after the nuke, so all 159 of its cases died at AttributeError BEFORE entering the op - 100 percent of the secret grade, invisible in every loud category. An agent following the prompt table literally ships green. I only found it by hand-cross-tabulating test_results.json failure messages by test file, which is not in the protocol.
suggest: Add a Testing Protocol step: after the CLI, group non-passing rows by test FILE and read the top failure messages, because no_axes_found rows carry real signal for the non-registry suites. Call out the specific killer - an AttributeError/ImportError in that bucket means the op is unreachable under the name a suite calls, not that the cell is unsupported. Better still, have verify_supported.py split no_axes_found by status and print a loud line when any of them are error/failed with an AttributeError.
